## Overview

ERPNext, by **Frappe Technologies**, is a 100% open-source ERP spanning inventory, manufacturing, accounting, sales, purchasing and CRM. For the Cycle Motion uplift it is the open-source peer of Odoo — a **Path 2/Path 3** contender with strong manufacturing/BOM capability. Like Odoo, it ships its own accounting and has **no native MYOB AccountRight connector**, so an "ERPNext with MYOB" architecture reintroduces middleware in the idempotent-sync critical path, plus open-source self-maintenance. It is recorded to keep the open-source field complete; it is not recommended ahead of the MYOB-native options for this brief.

## Products & Services

- **Manufacturing**: multi-level BOMs (finished goods and sub-assemblies), work orders, production planning, material consumption, capacity planning, subcontracting.
- **Inventory/WMS**: multi-warehouse, barcode, batch/serial.
- **eCommerce**: Shopify and other connectors available.
- **Accounting**: its own accounting module (so MYOB is redundant in a Path 3 framing).
- **MYOB integration**: no native connector; middleware/custom only (e.g. Integrator.io's generic AccountRight connector).

## Pricing Model

Open-source (Frappe/ERPNext, GPL/MIT-family) — free to self-host; **Frappe Cloud** offers managed hosting subscriptions. As with any open-source ERP, the real cost is implementation-partner effort plus ongoing self-maintenance (hosting, upgrades, patching, connector upkeep). Indicative TCO is comparable to the Odoo Community scenario and dominated by partner scope; treat as a range pending G-6.

## Strengths

- Strong, genuinely deep manufacturing: multi-level BOM, work orders, capacity planning, subcontracting.
- Fully open-source — no licence lock-in; open data; large global community.
- Multi-warehouse + barcode inventory; Shopify/Magento connectors available.

## Weaknesses

- No native MYOB AccountRight connector — middleware/custom in the idempotent-sync critical path (same caveat as Odoo; tensions Principles 9 and 10).
- Open-source self-maintenance (hosting, upgrades, patching, connector upkeep) — tensions Principle 1 and the brief's "no maintenance treadmill" stance.
- ERP-scale change, heavier than the brief's minimal-disruption intent; smaller AU partner ecosystem than Odoo.
